questions.question: Which pattern most strongly suggests inflammatory synovitis rather than typical mechanical OA?
choices: Persistent swollen small joints with prolonged morning stiffness that improves with movement
Pain only after a single marathon
Brief stiffness with bony DIP enlargement only
No symptoms but an incidental x-ray finding
questions.explanation: Persistent small-joint swelling and prolonged morning stiffness that improves with activity are features of inflammatory arthritis and warrant prompt assessment.

questions.question: A patient receiving a biologic has fever and one hot, swollen knee with inability to bear weight. What is the best next step?
choices: Assume RA flare and inject the joint
Urgent evaluation for septic arthritis and crystal disease
Add a long-term opioid
Wait for antibody results
questions.explanation: A hot swollen monoarthritis with fever, especially in an immunomodulated patient, may be septic arthritis. It requires urgent evaluation and often aspiration; do not assume flare.

questions.question: What is the role of anti-CCP or rheumatoid factor in suspected RA?
choices: Each test alone diagnoses RA
They support probability in a compatible clinical pattern but do not replace the history and examination
They rule out RA when negative
They identify septic arthritis
questions.explanation: Serology informs probability. Positive results can occur outside RA, and seronegative RA exists; diagnosis depends on the whole clinical pattern.

questions.question: Why are chronic NSAIDs alone inadequate disease treatment for active RA?
choices: They never reduce pain
They can reduce symptoms but do not prevent inflammatory joint damage
They cure RA permanently
They replace rheumatology referral
questions.explanation: NSAIDs may provide symptom relief but do not alter RA's immune-mediated disease process or prevent erosions. Disease-modifying strategy is needed.

questions.question: Which FNP action most supports a treat-to-target RA approach?
choices: Wait until joint deformity appears before referral
Document active synovitis and function, expedite rheumatology care, and support monitoring and adherence
Use repeated prednisone tapers indefinitely without a plan
Avoid vaccinations and prevention discussions
questions.explanation: Early rheumatology coordination and clear disease-activity documentation help initiate disease-modifying treatment before permanent damage occurs. FNP follow-up supports safe monitoring and access.

questions.question: Why should reproductive goals be reviewed before changing RA therapy?
choices: All RA drugs are interchangeable in pregnancy
Some treatments require pregnancy-specific timing or alternatives, while uncontrolled disease also carries risk
Pregnancy is unrelated to rheumatology care
It is only relevant after delivery
questions.explanation: Medication and disease control both affect pregnancy planning. Coordinate early with rheumatology and obstetrics rather than abruptly stopping essential therapy.

questions.question: Which finding is most useful to document separately during an inflammatory joint examination?
choices: Tender and swollen joint counts
Only the pain score
Only the patient's age
Only the x-ray report
questions.explanation: Tenderness and swelling provide different information; objective swelling is especially important for identifying synovitis and measuring trajectory.

questions.question: What is an important safety concern with repeated systemic glucocorticoid use?
choices: It guarantees remission without risks
Osteoporosis, hyperglycemia, hypertension, infection, and other harms can accumulate
It eliminates the need for vaccination review
It is a diagnostic test for RA
questions.explanation: Steroids may have a limited bridging role in selected plans, but repeated or chronic use produces substantial harm and should not replace disease-modifying treatment.

questions.question: Which new symptom in a patient with RA should not automatically be attributed to arthritis?
choices: Dyspnea and cough
Hand stiffness
Difficulty opening a jar
Symmetric MCP discomfort
questions.explanation: Dyspnea and cough may reflect infection, medication adverse effects, extra-articular disease, or unrelated illness. New systemic symptoms need separate assessment.

questions.question: Why are vaccine and infection-prevention discussions important in RA care?
choices: Immune-modifying therapy can change infection risk and vaccine timing or appropriateness
Vaccines always replace DMARDs
Only childhood vaccines matter
They are unrelated to medication safety
questions.explanation: DMARDs, biologics, and targeted agents may alter infection risk and vaccine planning. Coordinate preventive care using the exact therapy and current guidance.
